notes:
Snapshot: Ridgecrest Opsware — mid-market SaaS (product monitoring/observability for developer tools). Evaluated Redwood hosted API first, enthusiastic about latency and streaming UX. Current push: move to Redwood Dedicated for predictability (throughput + data isolation) and to meet customer data residency controls.

What they want / pain:
- Need consistent 95th pct latency <250ms for interactive code-assistant product under 50 RPS.
- Embedding pipeline: 100k vectors/day, must keep vector writes in-region and encrypted with customer-managed KMS.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget — prefers committed monthly capacity to reduce unit cost; wants clear overage rules.

Technical notes / PO C specifics:
- POC ran against hosted API (2 weeks) with Ridgecrest dataset (50k docs). Results: accuracy OK, but cost spikes during nightly batch reindexes; SE recommends Dedicated with batching and cache retention tuned.
- SE (Carlos) suggested auto-burst policy + cold-cache warm-up strategy; will provide Dedicated instance sizing spreadsheet (shared in Drive).
- Model preferences: want ability to route to quantized Llama-like variant for high-throughput reranking, fallback to higher-quality model for latency-insensitive requests.

Procurement / Legal asks (critical blockers):
- MSA redlines: Ridgecrest legal requests revision to liability cap, mutual indemnity, and explicit data segregation clause. "If we host customer data, vendor must certify no co-mingling."
- DPA: retention limits conflict with their in-house telemetry needs — they want 90-day min retention for debug logs; Redwood default is 30 days. Legal wants this in DPA.
- SLA: define uptime, measurement (region-level vs global), and SLA credit mechanics. Ridgecrest wants 99.9% per-region SLO for Dedicated endpoints.
- Security artifacts: SOC2 Type II report, ISO certs, pen-test summary, subprocessors list, certificate of insurance (COI). Procurement requested these before running vendor risk assessment.

Conversations & quotes:
- Procurement: "We can move quickly if MSA/DPA are reasonable — biggest hold is data residency + liability."
- Product lead: "If Dedicated gets us steady latencies under load, we can commit 12 months."

Commercial / pricing:
- AE proposed three options: 1) 12-month reserved pool (preferred by Ridgecrest), 2) 6-month trial committed, 3) hosted overage with cost cap.
- Ridgecrest requested a committed quote with clear SKU for burst capacity and quantization licensing. Est. ARR band $150k-$400k depending on burst SLA and retention add-ons.

Next steps (owner assignments):
- AE (Maya): circulate redlined MSA + SLA addendum by 2026-03-16; include COI & subprocessor list. (Action: attach redline doc to Drive)
- SE (Carlos): finalize Dedicated sizing and cost model; run one more load test against Dedicated staging by 2026-03-14; validate 95p latency <250ms under 50 RPS.
- Procurement (Ridgecrest): schedule vendor risk assessment with Redwood security week of 2026-03-17; legal to return DPA redlines.

Open blockers: MSA/DPA negotiation, retention windows on logs, SLA per-region language, insurance/certs. Ticket INF-3421 tracks SOC2/CISO artifact request.

CRM tidbits: short, choppy notes preferred by procurement team. Use Drive links above for artifacts. Follow-up cadence: weekly until MSA closed.
